messages:
sam: Quick flag — replay harness numbers are ~18% worse p95 than our synthetic closed-loop for the same QPS. Not sure if this is batch scheduling, kernel pick, or client churn. 🤔
ana: Can you paste the two configs? replay vs synthetic?
sam: Replay = production trace replay (burstiness preserved), 2000 qps avg, conn pool 150, keepalive on, 8 concurrent streams per conn. Synthetic = Poisson steady arrivals, conn pool 20, keepalive on, reuse conns always.
ravi: That already smells like connection churn differences. Replay keeps session affinity low so we get more TLS handshakes and shorter TCP warmup.
megan: Also the runtime's kernel selection prefers fwd-optimized kernels for short sequences; if replay has longer context tails we might be falling back to generic kernels more often.
perf-bot: perf-summary: hotspots: choose_kernel() 22.4% CPU, kv_cache_lookup() 17.8%, batch_builder.lock_wait 9.5%, tls_handshake 6.1% (measured during replay run).
joel: Do we have a timeline / flame for choose_kernel? is it expensive because of heuristics or because it collects seq-distribution stats every request?
ana: It samples every 100 requests currently. That together with frequent small batches could amplify overhead. We saw this in the last regression.
sam: I repro'd locally by toggling sampling to 1-in-1000 and p95 dropped to ~8% delta vs synthetic. So heuristics sampling cost is real.
ravi: Another artifact: replay had more prefix cache misses. KV cache hit-rate was 72% vs 93% in synthetic. That increases token work and changes kernel choices.
megan: Worth making two axis: (1) client-side connection behavior (keepalive, pool size, TLS churn, gRPC multiplexing) (2) server-side heuristics (kernel selection frequency, batch sizing, cache TTL). We should vary them independently.
joel: For client-side testing, please try: smaller conn pool + simulated TLS churn. Example harness tweak:
```
# replay harness config snippet
connection_pool: 30
keepalive: true
max_idle: 20s
tls_reconnect_window: 60s
grpc_max_concurrent_streams: 100
```
small changes made big diffs for me.
sam: FWIW toggling TCP_NODELAY on client reduced p95 by ~12ms in replay scenario. Nagle aggregation + TLS record coalescing seems to add ~1-2ms per request, but under our tail it amplifies.
ana: Did you measure with kernel-level batching? kernel selection can cause more small kernel launches which interact badly with TLS/Nagle.
perf-bot: microtrace excerpt:

---
REQUEST 12456: client_conn=143 tls_reuse=false kv_hit=false
choose_kernel -> generic (12us), batch_enqueue (37us), cuda_launch (120us)
TLS handshake (blocked) 2560us
---

Shows TLS handshake dominates certain traces.
ravi: So the story is layered: replay increases TLS/churn -> lower KV hit -> different kernel -> smaller batches -> higher per-token overhead -> higher p95.
megan: Actionable plan:
- run controlled matrix: keepalive=true/false, pool=20/150, tls_reconnect=off/60s, grpc vs rest
- server: sampling 1/100 vs 1/1000, disable auto kernel re-eval for warmup window, force larger batch target for comparison
- collect per-request tags: kv_hit, kernel_choice, conn_reuse, tls_reused
sam: Agree. Also add a synthetic trace that replays connection churn (not just request timing) so synthetic can mimic TLS churn. That'll give apples-to-apples.
joel: One more gotcha — our gRPC path multiplexes streams over a single HTTP/2 conn. That hides TCP/TLS costs in synthetic if you're reusing streams, but a replay with many ephemeral clients will show big difference. So test both gRPC and REST.
ana: I'm going to run the matrix overnight. Will tag runs with the metadata you asked. If anyone wants a specific combo, comment now.
megan: Please include a run with KV cache warmup disabled (start cold) and another with preloaded cache to see delta.
sam: Thx — also logging request-level kernel_choice in debug builds helped me correlate p95 with kernel shifts. We'll revert after.
perf-bot: scheduled job created: bench/replay-matrix/2026-05-12-overnight (includes conn churn variants, sampling toggles, kernel-lockouts).
joel: tiny note — disable Nagle (TCP_NODELAY) on the REST client when measuring latency-sensitive tails; for bandwidth-heavy tests keep it on.
ravi: On measuring TLS overhead, use openssl s_time or tcpdump to sanity check bytes per handshake. We had a case where ALPN negotiation added extra round-trips due to client hello size.
ana: Great points. I'll post the run summaries tomorrow morning. If we see persistent regression after the matrix, we should consider an interim mitigation: reduce sampling frequency and bias kernel re-eval to only after batch size > N.
sam: Sounds good. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
